items.excerpt: DeepMind says its WeatherNext model now predicts tropical cyclone track and intensity a full day further out than prior systems — a jump the team likens to roughly a decade of conventional forecasting progress. The model is being fed to national weather agencies for live storm season use.

University at Buffalo researchers pair Raman spectroscopy with a neural network to identify organelles inside living cells at about 90% accuracy — with no fluorescent dyes that perturb the cell. The 'Ramanomics' approach could let biologists watch cells without altering what they are watching.

OpenAI published ten AI-generated math results over a weekend; mathematicians now say several omit citations to existing prior work and amount to research misconduct rather than new discoveries. The dispute is becoming a test case for how AI-produced results get credited.

A Chinese team coupled a physics-guided neural network with machine learning to forecast typhoon wave heights, cutting error by 34.9% in one storm case. Hybrid physics-plus-ML models are steadily displacing pure numerical simulation in operational forecasting.

A study of multi-agent AI systems found a single misaligned agent can drag down the whole team's performance, and that its divergent reasoning stays largely invisible in its public messages. The work maps a failure mode for the agent swarms now being wired into research and product workflows.

Recursion and Genentech will co-develop a neuroscience program built on the first therapeutic target validated through Recursion's AI-driven 'maps of biology.' It is an early proof point that machine-generated target hypotheses can survive wet-lab validation.

MIT engineers built a dual-arm rehab robot that uses generative AI to learn from physical therapists and adapt its assistance to each stroke patient's force feedback. The system is framed as extending a therapist's reach rather than replacing the clinician.

A mathematician using Claude Fable 5 found a compact counterexample that topples the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture in three dimensions and above. The model's role was to search an enormous space of polynomial mappings the human then verified.

Schrödinger CEO Ramy Farid, a long-time physics-based simulation partisan, explains what changed his mind about machine learning in drug design. A rare on-record account of a computational-chemistry veteran revising his method stack.

New cognitive research suggests skills atrophy when AI does the work outright, but hold or improve when AI is used as a guide that keeps the learner's mind engaged. The distinction matters for anyone redesigning how their team works with models.

Northwestern, UChicago and Fermilab scientists deployed a deep-learning scheduler that decides what a telescope observes next, learning from historical logs instead of hand-coded rules. Across two observing runs it matched human schedulers while adapting live to changing sky conditions.

Quanta surveys mounting evidence that reasoning models often reach right answers through processes that do not match their stated chain of thought. The question of whether that is reasoning or sophisticated pattern matching now has real experimental stakes.

Machine learning applied to volatile organic compounds in exhaled breath separated tuberculosis patients from healthy controls with 93% accuracy. The method points to fast, non-invasive screening where lab infrastructure is scarce.

University of Maryland researchers released an open-access solid-state battery database — 245 records, 167 structured variables, 40,000+ data points — to fix the format chaos that blocks AI-guided battery design. Clean, structured data is the bottleneck before any model.

MIT researchers build AI 'future selves' — age-progressed avatars that talk users through hard life decisions. Early studies show real effects on choices, alongside warnings that the avatars encode their makers' assumptions.
